parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence: the former impersonation offence was removed in 2013 and presentation is lawful. No documented police targeting, violence pattern, or facility/custody exposure; absence of violence figures is treated as undocumented, not safety. A long-recognised third-gender role, chiefly inclusion, and an overview characterisation of society as very tolerant of trans people provide documented acceptance, a positive under burden-of-proof symmetry. The same-sex conduct statute is secondary under rule 2: it is tangential where trans tolerance is documented, though its non-enforcement rests on weak sourcing and use since 2013 is unresolved, so it remains a latent risk with no documented visitor-facing remedy operating e.g. compensation. Border, facilities and custody are open questions - light deductions, not known exposures. This places it a step below the 0.75 acceptance-with-working-protections tier.
